title: Validation of an LC-MS/MS method for the quantitation of phytosterols derived from Aloe vera gel
author: Nabeshima, Mizutani, et al.
materials: Liquid chromatography was performed using the Agilent Technology 1260 system equipped with a degasser, binary pump, multisampler, and column compartment. Chromatographic separation was performed on an Ascentis Express C18 HPLC column (2.1 × 100 mm, 2.7 μm particles; Sigma-Aldrich Supelco) with a guard column (2.1 × 5 mm, 2.7 μm particles; Sigma-Aldrich Supelco). The analytic conditions were as follows: injection volume, 10 μL; flow rate, 0.4 mL/min; column temperature, 50 °C; multisampler, 10 °C. Solvent A was acetonitrile/water (90:10 v/v) and solvent B was methanol/water/formic acid (900:100:1, v/v/v). The gradient program was as follows: solvent A 100%, solvent B 0% (0–8.5 min), solvent A 0%, solvent B 100% (8.5–24 min), and solvent A 100%, solvent B 0% (24–36 min).

steps.title: Prepare Aloe vera gel sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 g of AVGP (fine powder from dried Aloe vera mesophyll) into a 50 mL flask, add 40 mL of extraction solvent (chloroform : methanol, 2 : 1 v/v), sonicate 10 min at 25 °C, then bring the volume to 50 mL with the same solvent. Transfer 5 mL of the suspension to a centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 1150 × g, 25 °C for 5 min, and collect 2 mL of the supernatant. Evaporate the solvent at 40 °C under a nitrogen stream to dryness. Dissolve the residue in 20 mL methanol, sonicate 15 min at ambient temperature, and filter through a 0.22 µm PVDF filter (Tomsic, Japan) to obtain the measurement sample.

steps.title: Set up LC system and column
steps.instruction: Install the Agilent 1260 LC system (degasser, binary pump, multisampler, column compartment). Mount an Ascentis Express C18 column (2.1 × 100 mm, 2.7 µm particles, Sigma‑Aldrich Supelco) with a guard column (2.1 × 5 mm, 2.7 µm particles, Sigma‑Aldrich Supelco). Set injection volume to 10 µL, flow rate to 0.4 mL/min, column temperature to 50 °C, and multisampler temperature to 10 °C.

steps.title: Prepare mobile phases and gradient
steps.instruction: Prepare Solvent A as acetonitrile : water (90 : 10 v/v) and Solvent B as methanol : water : formic acid (900 : 100 : 1 v/v/v). Program the gradient: 0–8.5 min, 100 % A / 0 % B; 8.5–24 min, 0 % A / 100 % B; 24–36 min, return to 100 % A / 0 % B.

steps.title: Configure MS/MS parameters
steps.instruction: Connect the Agilent 6460 Triple Quad LC/MS. Set nebulizer pressure to 20 psi, drying gas flow to 4 mL/min, drying gas temperature to 325 °C, capillary voltage to 4500 V, and use nitrogen as the collision gas. Use the compound‑specific MS/MS settings from Table 1:

substeps.instruction: Lophenol: precursor m/z 383.5 → product m/z 301, fragmentor 12 V, collision energy 15 V, positive polarity.
24‑Methyl‑lophenol: precursor m/z 397.4 → product m/z 315, fragmentor 18 V, collision energy 15 V, positive polarity.
24‑Ethyl‑lophenol: precursor m/z 411.6 → product m/z 417, fragmentor 11 V, collision energy 7 V, positive polarity.
Cycloartanol: precursor m/z 429.8 → product m/z 191, fragmentor 11 V, collision energy 15 V, positive polarity.
24‑Methylene‑cycloartanol: precursor m/z 441.1 → product m/z 191, fragmentor 16 V, collision energy 18 V, positive polarity.

steps.title: Generate calibration curve for linearity
steps.instruction: Prepare calibration standards at 10, 20, 40, 80, and 160 ng/mL. Inject each standard under the LC‑MS/MS conditions and record the peak areas. Plot concentration versus peak area and calculate the coefficient of determination (R²) to assess linearity.

steps.title: Determine LOQ and RSD at 10 ng/mL
steps.instruction: Inject the 10 ng/mL calibration standard five times. Calculate the standard deviation of the five responses, compute the limit of quantification as 10 × signal‑to‑noise (S/N) ratio, and determine the relative standard deviation (RSD).

steps.title: Perform recovery test and calculate recovery
steps.instruction: Spike a known amount of standard into a sample, measure the spiked sample and the unspiked sample, then compute recovery using: Recovery (%) = (C_spiked – C_sample) / C_standard × 100, where C_spiked is the concentration after spiking, C_sample is the original sample concentration, and C_standard is the concentration of the added standard.

steps.title: Assess method precision (repeatability & intermediate)
steps.instruction: Repeatability: analyze the same measurement sample five times on the same day and calculate the RSD. Intermediate precision: prepare and analyze two replicates per day on six different days (total n = 12) and calculate the RSD across all runs.

description: Linearity The solutions of calibration standard (10, 20, 40, 80, and 160 ng/mL) were used to build the calibration curve and its coefficient of determination was calculated. Calculation of the limit of quantification and relative standard deviation (RSD) The calibration standard (10 ng/mL) was analyzed five times to calculate the standard deviation, limit of quantification (10 S/N) [12], and RSD. Recovery test A recovery test was performed to confirm the accuracy of this method. Recovery was calculated as follows: Recovery (%) = (C spiked – C sample) / C standard × 100 C spiked: concentration of the sample to be spiked C sample: concentration of the sample C standard: concentration of the standard Precision The method precision was assessed by repeatability and intermediate precision. The repeatability was calculated by measuring the same sample 5 times on the same day. The intermediate precision was determined by the results of samples (n = 2 /day) prepared and analyzed on six different days. The RSDs were calculated.
